8678|    /*!
8679|    @brief an iterator for primitive JSON types
8680|
8681|    This class models an iterator for primitive JSON types (boolean, number,
8682|    string). It's only purpose is to allow the iterator/const_iterator classes
8683|    to "iterate" over primitive values. Internally, the iterator is modeled by
8684|    a `difference_type` variable. Value begin_value (`0`) models the begin,
8685|    end_value (`1`) models past the end.
8686|    */
8687|    class primitive_iterator_t
8688|    {
8689|      public:
8690|
8691|        difference_type get_value() const noexcept
8692|        {
8693|            return m_it;
8694|        }
8695|        /// set iterator to a defined beginning
8696|        void set_begin() noexcept
8697|        {
8698|            m_it = begin_value;
8699|        }
8700|
8701|        /// set iterator to a defined past the end
8702|        void set_end() noexcept
8703|        {
8704|            m_it = end_value;
8705|        }
8706|
8707|        /// return whether the iterator can be dereferenced
8708|        constexpr bool is_begin() const noexcept
8709|        {
8710|            return (m_it == begin_value);
8711|        }
8712|
8713|        /// return whether the iterator is at end
8714|        constexpr bool is_end() const noexcept
8715|        {
8716|            return (m_it == end_value);
8717|        }
8718|
8719|        friend constexpr bool operator==(primitive_iterator_t lhs, primitive_iterator_t rhs) noexcept
8720|        {
8721|            return lhs.m_it == rhs.m_it;
8722|        }
8723|
8724|        friend constexpr bool operator!=(primitive_iterator_t lhs, primitive_iterator_t rhs) noexcept
8725|        {
8726|            return !(lhs == rhs);
8727|        }
8728|
8729|        friend constexpr bool operator<(primitive_iterator_t lhs, primitive_iterator_t rhs) noexcept
8730|        {
8731|            return lhs.m_it < rhs.m_it;
8732|        }
8733|
8734|        friend constexpr bool operator<=(primitive_iterator_t lhs, primitive_iterator_t rhs) noexcept
8735|        {
8736|            return lhs.m_it <= rhs.m_it;
8737|        }
8738|
8739|        friend constexpr bool operator>(primitive_iterator_t lhs, primitive_iterator_t rhs) noexcept
8740|        {
8741|            return lhs.m_it > rhs.m_it;
8742|        }
8743|
8744|        friend constexpr bool operator>=(primitive_iterator_t lhs, primitive_iterator_t rhs) noexcept
8745|        {
8746|            return lhs.m_it >= rhs.m_it;
8747|        }
8748|
8749|        primitive_iterator_t operator+(difference_type i)
8750|        {
8751|            auto result = *this;
8752|            result += i;
8753|            return result;
8754|        }
8755|
8756|        friend constexpr difference_type operator-(primitive_iterator_t lhs, primitive_iterator_t rhs) noexcept
8757|        {
8758|            return lhs.m_it - rhs.m_it;
8759|        }
8760|
8761|        friend std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, primitive_iterator_t it)
8762|        {
8763|            return os << it.m_it;
8764|        }
8765|
8766|        primitive_iterator_t& operator++()
8767|        {
8768|            ++m_it;
8769|            return *this;
8770|        }
8771|
8772|        primitive_iterator_t operator++(int)
8773|        {
8774|            auto result = *this;
8775|            m_it++;
8776|            return result;
8777|        }
8778|
8779|        primitive_iterator_t& operator--()
8780|        {
8781|            --m_it;
8782|            return *this;
8783|        }
8784|
8785|        primitive_iterator_t operator--(int)
8786|        {
8787|            auto result = *this;
8788|            m_it--;
8789|            return result;
8790|        }
8791|
8792|        primitive_iterator_t& operator+=(difference_type n)
8793|        {
8794|            m_it += n;
8795|            return *this;
8796|        }
8797|
8798|        primitive_iterator_t& operator-=(difference_type n)
8799|        {
8800|            m_it -= n;
8801|            return *this;
8802|        }
8803|
8804|      private:
8805|        static constexpr difference_type begin_value = 0;
8806|        static constexpr difference_type end_value = begin_value + 1;
8807|
8808|        /// iterator as signed integer type
8809|        difference_type m_it = std::numeric_limits<std::ptrdiff_t>::denorm_min();
8810|    };

8816|    allow unions members with complex constructors, see
8817|    https://github.com/nlohmann/json/pull/105.

8819|    struct internal_iterator
8820|    {

8834|    /// proxy class for the iterator_wrapper functions
8835|    template<typename IteratorType>
8836|    class iteration_proxy
8837|    {
8838|      private:
8839|        /// helper class for iteration
8840|        class iteration_proxy_internal
8841|        {
8842|          private:
8843|            /// the iterator
8844|            IteratorType anchor;
8845|            /// an index for arrays (used to create key names)
8846|            size_t array_index = 0;
8847|
8848|          public:
8849|            explicit iteration_proxy_internal(IteratorType it) noexcept
8850|                : anchor(it)
8851|            {}
8852|
8853|            /// dereference operator (needed for range-based for)
8854|            iteration_proxy_internal& operator*()
8855|            {
8856|                return *this;
8857|            }
8858|
8859|            /// increment operator (needed for range-based for)
8860|            iteration_proxy_internal& operator++()
8861|            {
8862|                ++anchor;
8863|                ++array_index;
8864|
8865|                return *this;
8866|            }
8867|
8868|            /// inequality operator (needed for range-based for)
8869|            bool operator!= (const iteration_proxy_internal& o) const
8870|            {
8871|                return anchor != o.anchor;
8872|            }
8873|
8874|            /// return key of the iterator
8875|            typename basic_json::string_t key() const
8876|            {
8877|                assert(anchor.m_object != nullptr);
8878|
8879|                switch (anchor.m_object->type())
8880|                {
8881|                    // use integer array index as key
8882|                    case value_t::array:
8883|                    {
8884|                        return std::to_string(array_index);
8885|                    }
8886|
8887|                    // use key from the object
8888|                    case value_t::object:
8889|                    {
8890|                        return anchor.key();
8891|                    }
8892|
8893|                    // use an empty key for all primitive types
8894|                    default:
8895|                    {
8896|                        return "";
8897|                    }
8898|                }
8899|            }
8900|
8901|            /// return value of the iterator
8902|            typename IteratorType::reference value() const
8903|            {
8904|                return anchor.value();
8905|            }
8906|        };
8907|
8908|        /// the container to iterate
8909|        typename IteratorType::reference container;
8910|
8911|      public:
8912|        /// construct iteration proxy from a container
8913|        explicit iteration_proxy(typename IteratorType::reference cont)
8914|            : container(cont)
8915|        {}
8916|
8917|        /// return iterator begin (needed for range-based for)
8918|        iteration_proxy_internal begin() noexcept
8919|        {
8920|            return iteration_proxy_internal(container.begin());
8921|        }
8922|
8923|        /// return iterator end (needed for range-based for)
8924|        iteration_proxy_internal end() noexcept
8925|        {
8926|            return iteration_proxy_internal(container.end());
8927|        }
8928|    };

8931|    /*!
8932|    @brief a template for a random access iterator for the @ref basic_json class
8933|
8934|    This class implements a both iterators (iterator and const_iterator) for the
8935|    @ref basic_json class.
8936|
8937|    @note An iterator is called *initialized* when a pointer to a JSON value
8938|          has been set (e.g., by a constructor or a copy assignment). If the
8939|          iterator is default-constructed, it is *uninitialized* and most
8940|          methods are undefined. **The library uses assertions to detect calls
8941|          on uninitialized iterators.**

8943|    @requirement The class satisfies the following concept requirements:
8944|    - [RandomAccessIterator](http://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/concept/RandomAccessIterator):
8945|      The iterator that can be moved to point (forward and backward) to any
8946|      element in constant time.

8948|    @since version 1.0.0, simplified in version 2.0.9

8957|        static_assert(std::is_same<U, basic_json>::value

8959|                      "iter_impl only accepts (const) basic_json");

8961|      public:
8962|        /// the type of the values when the iterator is dereferenced
8963|        using value_type = typename basic_json::value_type;
8964|        /// a type to represent differences between iterators
8965|        using difference_type = typename basic_json::difference_type;
8966|        /// defines a pointer to the type iterated over (value_type)
8967|        using pointer = typename std::conditional<std::is_const<U>::value,
8968|              typename basic_json::const_pointer,
8969|              typename basic_json::pointer>::type;
8970|        /// defines a reference to the type iterated over (value_type)
8971|        using reference = typename std::conditional<std::is_const<U>::value,
8972|              typename basic_json::const_reference,
8973|              typename basic_json::reference>::type;

8975|        using iterator_category = std::bidirectional_iterator_tag;

8977|        /// default constructor
8978|        iter_impl() = default;
8979|
8980|        /*!
8981|        @brief constructor for a given JSON instance
8982|        @param[in] object  pointer to a JSON object for this iterator
8983|        @pre object != nullptr
8984|        @post The iterator is initialized; i.e. `m_object != nullptr`.
8985|        */
8986|        explicit iter_impl(pointer object) noexcept
8987|            : m_object(object)
8988|        {
8989|            assert(m_object != nullptr);
8990|
8991|            switch (m_object->m_type)
8992|            {
8993|                case basic_json::value_t::object:
8994|                {
8995|                    m_it.object_iterator = typename object_t::iterator();
8996|                    break;
8997|                }
8998|
8999|                case basic_json::value_t::array:
9000|                {
9001|                    m_it.array_iterator = typename array_t::iterator();
9002|                    break;
9003|                }
9004|
9005|                default:
9006|                {
9007|                    m_it.primitive_iterator = primitive_iterator_t();

9016|        @ref const_iterator.

9019|        class is a @ref const_iterator this function is not called.

9022|        {

9736|        /*!
9737|        @brief create a string from one or two Unicode code points
9738|

9741|        @a codepoint1 and @a codepoint2 are a UTF-16 surrogate pair to

9745|        @param[in] codepoint2  the code point (can be low surrogate or 0)

9748|        result string is between 1 and 4 characters.

9751|        points above 0x10FFFF are invalid"`
9752|        @throw std::invalid_argument if the low surrogate is invalid; example:
9753|        `""missing or wrong low surrogate""`
9754|
9755|        @complexity Constant.
9756|

9758|        */

9760|                                   const std::size_t codepoint2 = 0)
9761|        {
9762|            // calculate the code point from the given code points
9763|            std::size_t codepoint = codepoint1;
9764|
9765|            // check if codepoint1 is a high surrogate
9766|            if (codepoint1 >= 0xD800 and codepoint1 <= 0xDBFF)
9767|            {
9768|                // check if codepoint2 is a low surrogate
9769|                if (codepoint2 >= 0xDC00 and codepoint2 <= 0xDFFF)
9770|                {
9771|                    codepoint =
9772|                        // high surrogate occupies the most significant 22 bits
9773|                        (codepoint1 << 10)
9774|                        // low surrogate occupies the least significant 15 bits
9775|                        + codepoint2
9776|                        // there is still the 0xD800, 0xDC00 and 0x10000 noise
9777|                        // in the result so we have to subtract with:
9778|                        // (0xD800 << 10) + DC00 - 0x10000 = 0x35FDC00
9779|                        - 0x35FDC00;
9780|                }

9782|                {
9783|                    JSON_THROW(std::invalid_argument("missing or wrong low surrogate"));
9784|                }

9804|                result.append(1, static_cast<typename string_t::value_type>(0x80 | ((codepoint >> 6) & 0x3F)));
9805|                result.append(1, static_cast<typename string_t::value_type>(0x80 | (codepoint & 0x3F)));
9806|            }
9807|            else if (codepoint <= 0x10ffff)
9808|            {
9809|                // 4-byte characters: 11110xxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx
9810|                result.append(1, static_cast<typename string_t::value_type>(0xF0 | ((codepoint >> 18) & 0x07)));
9811|                result.append(1, static_cast<typename string_t::value_type>(0x80 | ((codepoint >> 12) & 0x3F)));
9812|                result.append(1, static_cast<typename string_t::value_type>(0x80 | ((codepoint >> 6) & 0x3F)));
9813|                result.append(1, static_cast<typename string_t::value_type>(0x80 | (codepoint & 0x3F)));

11079|        of i is strictly increasing with each iteration, as it is incremented

11106|                        result.push_back(static_cast<typename string_t::value_type>(*k));

11111|                {

11113|                    // read next character
11114|                    ++i;

11119|                        case 't':

11123|                        }

11128|                        }

11132|                            break;
11133|                        }
11134|                        case 'n':

11137|                            break;
11138|                        }
11139|                        case 'r':
11140|                        {
11141|                            result += "\r";
11142|                            break;
11143|                        }
11144|                        case '\\':
11145|                        {
11146|                            result += "\\";

11251|            static void strtof(long double& f, const char* str, char** endptr)

11256|            template<typename T>
11257|            bool parse(T& value, /*is_integral=*/std::false_type) const
11258|            {

11260|                // when necessary; data will point to either the original
11261|                // string, or buf, or tempstr containing the fixed string.
11262|                std::string tempstr;
11263|                std::array<char, 64> buf;
11264|                const size_t len = static_cast<size_t>(m_end - m_start);
11265|
11266|                // lexer will reject empty numbers
11267|                assert(len > 0);
11268|
11269|                // since dealing with strtod family of functions, we're
11270|                // getting the decimal point char from the C locale facilities
11271|                // instead of C++'s numpunct facet of the current std::locale
11272|                const auto loc = localeconv();
11273|                assert(loc != nullptr);
11274|                const char decimal_point_char = (loc->decimal_point == nullptr) ? '.' : loc->decimal_point[0];
11275|
11276|                const char* data = m_start;
11277|
11278|                if (decimal_point_char != '.')
11279|                {
11280|                    const size_t ds_pos = static_cast<size_t>(std::find(m_start, m_end, '.') - m_start);
11281|
11282|                    if (ds_pos != len)
11283|                    {
11284|                        // copy the data into the local buffer or tempstr, if
11285|                        // buffer is too small; replace decimal separator, and
11286|                        // update data to point to the modified bytes
11287|                        if ((len + 1) < buf.size())
11288|                        {
11289|                            std::copy(m_start, m_end, buf.begin());
11290|                            buf[len] = 0;
11291|                            buf[ds_pos] = decimal_point_char;
11292|                            data = buf.data();
11293|                        }
11294|                        else
11295|                        {
11296|                            tempstr.assign(m_start, m_end);
11297|                            tempstr[ds_pos] = decimal_point_char;
11298|                            data = tempstr.c_str();
11299|                        }
11300|                    }
11301|                }
11302|
11303|                char* endptr = nullptr;
11304|                value = 0;
11305|                // this calls appropriate overload depending on T
11306|                strtof(value, data, &endptr);
11307|
11308|                // parsing was successful iff strtof parsed exactly the number
11309|                // of characters determined by the lexer (len)
11310|                const bool ok = (endptr == (data + len));
11311|
11312|                if (ok and (value == static_cast<T>(0.0)) and (*data == '-'))
11313|                {
11314|                    // some implementations forget to negate the zero
11315|                    value = -0.0;
11316|                }
11317|
11318|                return ok;
11319|            }
11320|
11321|            // integral conversion
11322|
11323|            signed long long parse_integral(char** endptr, /*is_signed*/std::true_type) const
11324|            {
11325|                return std::strtoll(m_start, endptr, 10);
11326|            }
11327|
11328|            unsigned long long parse_integral(char** endptr, /*is_signed*/std::false_type) const
11329|            {
11330|                return std::strtoull(m_start, endptr, 10);
11331|            }
11332|
11333|            template<typename T>
11334|            bool parse(T& value, /*is_integral=*/std::true_type) const
11335|            {
11336|                char* endptr = nullptr;
11337|                errno = 0; // these are thread-local
11338|                const auto x = parse_integral(&endptr, std::is_signed<T>());
11339|
11340|                // called right overload?
11341|                static_assert(std::is_signed<T>() == std::is_signed<decltype(x)>(), "");
11342|
11343|                value = static_cast<T>(x);
11344|
11345|                return (x == static_cast<decltype(x)>(value)) // x fits into destination T
11346|                       and (x < 0) == (value < 0)             // preserved sign
11347|                       //and ((x != 0) or is_integral())        // strto[u]ll did nto fail
11348|                       and (errno == 0)                       // strto[u]ll did not overflow
11349|                       and (m_start < m_end)                  // token was not empty
11350|                       and (endptr == m_end);                 // parsed entire token exactly
11351|            }

11354|        /*!
11355|        @brief return number value for number tokens
11356|
11357|        This function translates the last token into the most appropriate
11358|        number type (either integer, unsigned integer or floating point),
11359|        which is passed back to the caller via the result parameter.
11360|
11361|        integral numbers that don't fit into the the range of the respective
11362|        type are parsed as number_float_t
11363|
11364|        floating-point values do not satisfy std::isfinite predicate
11365|        are converted to value_t::null
11366|
11367|        throws if the entire string [m_start .. m_cursor) cannot be
11368|        interpreted as a number
11369|
11370|        @param[out] result  @ref basic_json object to receive the number.
11371|        @param[in]  token   the type of the number token
11372|        */
11373|        bool get_number(basic_json& result, const token_type token) const
11374|        {
11375|            assert(m_start != nullptr);
11376|            assert(m_start < m_cursor);
11377|            assert((token == token_type::value_unsigned) or
11378|                   (token == token_type::value_integer) or
11379|                   (token == token_type::value_float));
11380|
11381|            strtonum num_converter(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(m_start),
11382|                                   reinterpret_cast<const char*>(m_cursor));
11383|
11384|            switch (token)
11385|            {
11386|                case lexer::token_type::value_unsigned:
11387|                {
11388|                    number_unsigned_t val;
11389|                    if (num_converter.to(val))
11390|                    {
11391|                        // parsing successful
11392|                        result.m_type = value_t::number_unsigned;
11393|                        result.m_value = val;
11394|                        return true;
11395|                    }
11396|                    break;
11397|                }
11398|
11399|                case lexer::token_type::value_integer:
11400|                {
11401|                    number_integer_t val;
11402|                    if (num_converter.to(val))
11403|                    {
11404|                        // parsing successful
11405|                        result.m_type = value_t::number_integer;
11406|                        result.m_value = val;
11407|                        return true;
11408|                    }
11409|                    break;
11410|                }
11411|
11412|                default:
11413|                {
11414|                    break;
11415|                }
11416|            }
11417|
11418|            // parse float (either explicitly or because a previous conversion
11419|            // failed)
11420|            number_float_t val;
11421|            if (num_converter.to(val))
11422|            {
11423|                // parsing successful
11424|                result.m_type = value_t::number_float;
11425|                result.m_value = val;
11426|
11427|                // throw in case of infinity or NAN
11428|                if (not std::isfinite(result.m_value.number_float))
11429|                {
11430|                    JSON_THROW(std::out_of_range("number overflow: " + get_token_string()));
11431|                }
11432|
11433|                return true;
11434|            }
11435|
11436|            // couldn't parse number in any format
11437|            return false;
11438|        }

11461|    /*!
11462|    @brief syntax analysis
11463|
11464|    This class implements a recursive decent parser.
11465|    */
11466|    class parser
11467|    {
11468|      public:
11469|        /// a parser reading from a string literal
11470|        parser(const char* buff, const parser_callback_t cb = nullptr)
11471|            : callback(cb),
11472|              m_lexer(reinterpret_cast<const typename lexer::lexer_char_t*>(buff), std::strlen(buff))
11473|        {}
11474|
11475|        /// a parser reading from an input stream
11476|        parser(std::istream& is, const parser_callback_t cb = nullptr)
11477|            : callback(cb), m_lexer(is)
11478|        {}
11479|
11480|        /// a parser reading from an iterator range with contiguous storage
11481|        template<class IteratorType, typename std::enable_if<
11482|                     std::is_same<typename std::iterator_traits<IteratorType>::iterator_category, std::random_access_iterator_tag>::value
11483|                     , int>::type
11484|                 = 0>
11485|        parser(IteratorType first, IteratorType last, const parser_callback_t cb = nullptr)
11486|            : callback(cb),
11487|              m_lexer(reinterpret_cast<const typename lexer::lexer_char_t*>(&(*first)),
11488|                      static_cast<size_t>(std::distance(first, last)))
11489|        {}
11490|
11491|        /// public parser interface
11492|        basic_json parse()
11493|        {
11494|            // read first token
11495|            get_token();
11496|
11497|            basic_json result = parse_internal(true);
11498|            result.assert_invariant();
11499|
11500|            expect(lexer::token_type::end_of_input);
11501|
11502|            // return parser result and replace it with null in case the
11503|            // top-level value was discarded by the callback function
11504|            return result.is_discarded() ? basic_json() : std::move(result);
11505|        }
11506|
11507|      private:
11508|        /// the actual parser
11509|        basic_json parse_internal(bool keep)
11510|        {
11511|            auto result = basic_json(value_t::discarded);
11512|
11513|            switch (last_token)
11514|            {
11515|                case lexer::token_type::begin_object:
11516|                {
11517|                    if (keep and (not callback
11518|                                  or ((keep = callback(depth++, parse_event_t::object_start, result)) != 0)))
11519|                    {
11520|                        // explicitly set result to object to cope with {}
11521|                        result.m_type = value_t::object;
11522|                        result.m_value = value_t::object;
11523|                    }
11524|
11525|                    // read next token
11526|                    get_token();
11527|
11528|                    // closing } -> we are done
11529|                    if (last_token == lexer::token_type::end_object)
11530|                    {
11531|                        get_token();
11532|                        if (keep and callback and not callback(--depth, parse_event_t::object_end, result))
11533|                        {
11534|                            result = basic_json(value_t::discarded);
11535|                        }
11536|                        return result;
11537|                    }
11538|
11539|                    // no comma is expected here
11540|                    unexpect(lexer::token_type::value_separator);
11541|
11542|                    // otherwise: parse key-value pairs
11543|                    do
11544|                    {
11545|                        // ugly, but could be fixed with loop reorganization
11546|                        if (last_token == lexer::token_type::value_separator)
11547|                        {
11548|                            get_token();
11549|                        }
11550|
11551|                        // store key
11552|                        expect(lexer::token_type::value_string);
11553|                        const auto key = m_lexer.get_string();
11554|
11555|                        bool keep_tag = false;
11556|                        if (keep)
11557|                        {
11558|                            if (callback)
11559|                            {
11560|                                basic_json k(key);
11561|                                keep_tag = callback(depth, parse_event_t::key, k);
11562|                            }
11563|                            else
11564|                            {
11565|                                keep_tag = true;
11566|                            }
11567|                        }
11568|
11569|                        // parse separator (:)
11570|                        get_token();
11571|                        expect(lexer::token_type::name_separator);
11572|
11573|                        // parse and add value
11574|                        get_token();
11575|                        auto value = parse_internal(keep);
11576|                        if (keep and keep_tag and not value.is_discarded())
11577|                        {
11578|                            result[key] = std::move(value);
11579|                        }
11580|                    }
11581|                    while (last_token == lexer::token_type::value_separator);
11582|
11583|                    // closing }
11584|                    expect(lexer::token_type::end_object);
11585|                    get_token();
11586|                    if (keep and callback and not callback(--depth, parse_event_t::object_end, result))
11587|                    {
11588|                        result = basic_json(value_t::discarded);
11589|                    }
11590|
11591|                    return result;
11592|                }
11593|
11594|                case lexer::token_type::begin_array:
11595|                {
11596|                    if (keep and (not callback
11597|                                  or ((keep = callback(depth++, parse_event_t::array_start, result)) != 0)))
11598|                    {
11599|                        // explicitly set result to object to cope with []
11600|                        result.m_type = value_t::array;
11601|                        result.m_value = value_t::array;
11602|                    }
11603|
11604|                    // read next token
11605|                    get_token();
11606|
11607|                    // closing ] -> we are done
11608|                    if (last_token == lexer::token_type::end_array)
11609|                    {
11610|                        get_token();
11611|                        if (callback and not callback(--depth, parse_event_t::array_end, result))
11612|                        {
11613|                            result = basic_json(value_t::discarded);
11614|                        }
11615|                        return result;
11616|                    }
11617|
11618|                    // no comma is expected here
11619|                    unexpect(lexer::token_type::value_separator);
11620|
11621|                    // otherwise: parse values
11622|                    do
11623|                    {
11624|                        // ugly, but could be fixed with loop reorganization
11625|                        if (last_token == lexer::token_type::value_separator)
11626|                        {
11627|                            get_token();
11628|                        }
11629|
11630|                        // parse value
11631|                        auto value = parse_internal(keep);
11632|                        if (keep and not value.is_discarded())
11633|                        {
11634|                            result.push_back(std::move(value));
11635|                        }
11636|                    }
11637|                    while (last_token == lexer::token_type::value_separator);
11638|
11639|                    // closing ]
11640|                    expect(lexer::token_type::end_array);
11641|                    get_token();
11642|                    if (keep and callback and not callback(--depth, parse_event_t::array_end, result))
11643|                    {
11644|                        result = basic_json(value_t::discarded);
11645|                    }
11646|
11647|                    return result;
11648|                }
11649|
11650|                case lexer::token_type::literal_null:
11651|                {
11652|                    get_token();
11653|                    result.m_type = value_t::null;
11654|                    break;
11655|                }
11656|
11657|                case lexer::token_type::value_string:
11658|                {
11659|                    const auto s = m_lexer.get_string();
11660|                    get_token();
11661|                    result = basic_json(s);
11662|                    break;
11663|                }
11664|
11665|                case lexer::token_type::literal_true:
11666|                {
11667|                    get_token();
11668|                    result.m_type = value_t::boolean;
11669|                    result.m_value = true;
11670|                    break;
11671|                }
11672|
11673|                case lexer::token_type::literal_false:
11674|                {
11675|                    get_token();
11676|                    result.m_type = value_t::boolean;
11677|                    result.m_value = false;
11678|                    break;
11679|                }
11680|
11681|                case lexer::token_type::value_unsigned:
11682|                case lexer::token_type::value_integer:
11683|                case lexer::token_type::value_float:
11684|                {
11685|                    m_lexer.get_number(result, last_token);
11686|                    get_token();
11687|                    break;
11688|                }
11689|
11690|                default:
11691|                {
11692|                    // the last token was unexpected
11693|                    unexpect(last_token);
11694|                }
11695|            }
11696|
11697|            if (keep and callback and not callback(depth, parse_event_t::value, result))
11698|            {
11699|                result = basic_json(value_t::discarded);
11700|            }
11701|            return result;
11702|        }

11704|        /// get next token from lexer
11705|        typename lexer::token_type get_token()
11706|        {
11707|            last_token = m_lexer.scan();
11708|            return last_token;
11709|        }

11711|        void expect(typename lexer::token_type t) const
11712|        {
11713|            if (t != last_token)
11714|            {
11715|                std::string error_msg = "parse error - unexpected ";

11722|        }
11723|
11724|        void unexpect(typename lexer::token_type t) const
11725|        {
11726|            if (t == last_token)
11727|            {
11728|                std::string error_msg = "parse error - unexpected ";
11729|                error_msg += (last_token == lexer::token_type::parse_error ? ("'" +  m_lexer.get_token_string() +
11730|                              "'") :
11731|                              lexer::token_type_name(last_token));

11736|      private:
11737|        /// current level of recursion
11738|        int depth = 0;
11739|        /// callback function
11740|        const parser_callback_t callback = nullptr;
11741|        /// the type of the last read token
11742|        typename lexer::token_type last_token = lexer::token_type::uninitialized;
11743|        /// the lexer
11744|        lexer m_lexer;
11745|    };

11748|    /*!
11749|    @brief JSON Pointer
11750|
11751|    A JSON pointer defines a string syntax for identifying a specific value
11752|    within a JSON document. It can be used with functions `at` and
11753|    `operator[]`. Furthermore, JSON pointers are the base for JSON patches.

11758|    */
11759|    class json_pointer
11760|    {
11761|        /// allow basic_json to access private members
11762|        friend class basic_json;
11763|
11764|      public:
11765|        /*!
11766|        @brief create JSON pointer
11767|
11768|        Create a JSON pointer according to the syntax described in
11769|        [Section 3 of RFC6901](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901#section-3).
11770|
11771|        @param[in] s  string representing the JSON pointer; if omitted, the
11772|                      empty string is assumed which references the whole JSON
11773|                      value
11774|
11775|        @throw std::domain_error if reference token is nonempty and does not
11776|        begin with a slash (`/`); example: `"JSON pointer must be empty or
11777|        begin with /"`
11778|        @throw std::domain_error if a tilde (`~`) is not followed by `0`
11779|        (representing `~`) or `1` (representing `/`); example: `"escape error:
11780|        ~ must be followed with 0 or 1"`
11781|
11782|        @liveexample{The example shows the construction several valid JSON
11783|        pointers as well as the exceptional behavior.,json_pointer}
11784|
11785|        @since version 2.0.0
11786|        */
11787|        explicit json_pointer(const std::string& s = "")
11788|            : reference_tokens(split(s))
11789|        {}
11790|
11791|        /*!
11792|        @brief return a string representation of the JSON pointer
11793|
11794|        @invariant For each JSON pointer `ptr`, it holds:
11795|        @code {.cpp}
11796|        ptr == json_pointer(ptr.to_string());
11797|        @endcode
11798|
11799|        @return a string representation of the JSON pointer
11800|
11801|        @liveexample{The example shows the result of `to_string`.,
11802|        json_pointer__to_string}
11803|
11804|        @since version 2.0.0
11805|        */
11806|        std::string to_string() const noexcept
11807|        {
11808|            return std::accumulate(reference_tokens.begin(),
11809|                                   reference_tokens.end(), std::string{},
11810|                                   [](const std::string & a, const std::string & b)
11811|            {
11812|                return a + "/" + escape(b);
11813|            });
11814|        }
11815|
11816|        /// @copydoc to_string()
11817|        operator std::string() const
11818|        {
11819|            return to_string();
11820|        }

11822|      private:
11823|        /// remove and return last reference pointer
11824|        std::string pop_back()
11825|        {
11826|            if (is_root())
11827|            {
11828|                JSON_THROW(std::domain_error("JSON pointer has no parent"));
11829|            }
11830|
11831|            auto last = reference_tokens.back();
11832|            reference_tokens.pop_back();

11834|        }

11838|        {
11839|            return reference_tokens.empty();
11840|        }
11841|
11842|        json_pointer top() const
11843|        {
11844|            if (is_root())
11845|            {
11846|                JSON_THROW(std::domain_error("JSON pointer has no parent"));
11847|            }
11848|

11854|        /*!
11855|        @brief create and return a reference to the pointed to value

11859|        reference get_and_create(reference j) const
11860|        {
11861|            pointer result = &j;
11862|
11863|            // in case no reference tokens exist, return a reference to the
11864|            // JSON value j which will be overwritten by a primitive value
11865|            for (const auto& reference_token : reference_tokens)
11866|            {

11869|                    case value_t::null:
11870|                    {
11871|                        if (reference_token == "0")

11874|                            result = &result->operator[](0);
11875|                        }
11876|                        else
11877|                        {
11878|                            // start a new object otherwise
11879|                            result = &result->operator[](reference_token);
11880|                        }
11881|                        break;
11882|                    }
11883|
11884|                    case value_t::object:
11885|                    {
11886|                        // create an entry in the object
11887|                        result = &result->operator[](reference_token);
11888|                        break;
11889|                    }
11890|
11891|                    case value_t::array:
11892|                    {
11893|                        // create an entry in the array
11894|                        result = &result->operator[](static_cast<size_type>(std::stoi(reference_token)));

11897|
11898|                    /*
11899|                    The following code is only reached if there exists a
11900|                    reference token _and_ the current value is primitive. In
11901|                    this case, we have an error situation, because primitive
11902|                    values may only occur as single value; that is, with an
11903|                    empty list of reference tokens.
11904|                    */

11906|                    {
11907|                        JSON_THROW(std::domain_error("invalid value to unflatten"));
11908|                    }

12141|        /// split the string input to reference tokens
12142|        static std::vector<std::string> split(const std::string& reference_string)
12143|        {
12144|            std::vector<std::string> result;
12145|
12146|            // special case: empty reference string -> no reference tokens
12147|            if (reference_string.empty())
12148|            {
12149|                return result;
12150|            }
12151|
12152|            // check if nonempty reference string begins with slash
12153|            if (reference_string[0] != '/')
12154|            {
12155|                JSON_THROW(std::domain_error("JSON pointer must be empty or begin with '/'"));
12156|            }
12157|
12158|            // extract the reference tokens:
12159|            // - slash: position of the last read slash (or end of string)
12160|            // - start: position after the previous slash
12161|            for (
12162|                // search for the first slash after the first character
12163|                size_t slash = reference_string.find_first_of('/', 1),
12164|                // set the beginning of the first reference token
12165|                start = 1;
12166|                // we can stop if start == string::npos+1 = 0
12167|                start != 0;
12168|                // set the beginning of the next reference token
12169|                // (will eventually be 0 if slash == std::string::npos)
12170|                start = slash + 1,
12171|                // find next slash
12172|                slash = reference_string.find_first_of('/', start))
12173|            {
12174|                // use the text between the beginning of the reference token
12175|                // (start) and the last slash (slash).
12176|                auto reference_token = reference_string.substr(start, slash - start);
12177|
12178|                // check reference tokens are properly escaped
12179|                for (size_t pos = reference_token.find_first_of('~');
12180|                        pos != std::string::npos;
12181|                        pos = reference_token.find_first_of('~', pos + 1))
12182|                {
12183|                    assert(reference_token[pos] == '~');
12184|
12185|                    // ~ must be followed by 0 or 1
12186|                    if (pos == reference_token.size() - 1 or
12187|                            (reference_token[pos + 1] != '0' and
12188|                             reference_token[pos + 1] != '1'))
12189|                    {
12190|                        JSON_THROW(std::domain_error("escape error: '~' must be followed with '0' or '1'"));
12191|                    }
12192|                }
12193|
12194|                // finally, store the reference token
12195|                unescape(reference_token);
12196|                result.push_back(reference_token);
12197|            }
12198|
12199|            return result;
12200|        }

12202|      private:
12203|        /*!
12204|        @brief replace all occurrences of a substring by another string
12205|
12206|        @param[in,out] s  the string to manipulate; changed so that all
12207|                          occurrences of @a f are replaced with @a t
12208|        @param[in]     f  the substring to replace with @a t
12209|        @param[in]     t  the string to replace @a f
12210|
12211|        @pre The search string @a f must not be empty.
12212|
12213|        @since version 2.0.0
12214|        */
12215|        static void replace_substring(std::string& s,
12216|                                      const std::string& f,
12217|                                      const std::string& t)
12218|        {
12219|            assert(not f.empty());
12220|
12221|            for (
12222|                size_t pos = s.find(f);         // find first occurrence of f
12223|                pos != std::string::npos;       // make sure f was found
12224|                s.replace(pos, f.size(), t),    // replace with t
12225|                pos = s.find(f, pos + t.size()) // find next occurrence of f
12226|            );
12227|        }
12228|
12229|        /// escape tilde and slash
12230|        static std::string escape(std::string s)
12231|        {
12232|            // escape "~"" to "~0" and "/" to "~1"
12233|            replace_substring(s, "~", "~0");
12234|            replace_substring(s, "/", "~1");
12235|            return s;
12236|        }
12237|
12238|        /// unescape tilde and slash
12239|        static void unescape(std::string& s)
12240|        {
12241|            // first transform any occurrence of the sequence '~1' to '/'
12242|            replace_substring(s, "~1", "/");
12243|            // then transform any occurrence of the sequence '~0' to '~'
12244|            replace_substring(s, "~0", "~");
12245|        }

12247|        /*!
12248|        @param[in] reference_string  the reference string to the current value
12249|        @param[in] value             the value to consider
12250|        @param[in,out] result        the result object to insert values to
12251|
12252|        @note Empty objects or arrays are flattened to `null`.
12253|        */
12254|        static void flatten(const std::string& reference_string,
12255|                            const basic_json& value,
12256|                            basic_json& result)
12257|        {
12258|            switch (value.m_type)
12259|            {
12260|                case value_t::array:
12261|                {
12262|                    if (value.m_value.array->empty())
12263|                    {
12264|                        // flatten empty array as null
12265|                        result[reference_string] = nullptr;
12266|                    }
12267|                    else
12268|                    {
12269|                        // iterate array and use index as reference string
12270|                        for (size_t i = 0; i < value.m_value.array->size(); ++i)
12271|                        {
12272|                            flatten(reference_string + "/" + std::to_string(i),
12273|                                    value.m_value.array->operator[](i), result);
12274|                        }
12275|                    }
12276|                    break;
12277|                }
12278|
12279|                case value_t::object:
12280|                {
12281|                    if (value.m_value.object->empty())
12282|                    {
12283|                        // flatten empty object as null
12284|                        result[reference_string] = nullptr;
12285|                    }
12286|                    else
12287|                    {
12288|                        // iterate object and use keys as reference string
12289|                        for (const auto& element : *value.m_value.object)
12290|                        {
12291|                            flatten(reference_string + "/" + escape(element.first),
12292|                                    element.second, result);
12293|                        }
12294|                    }
12295|                    break;
12296|                }
12297|
12298|                default:
12299|                {
12300|                    // add primitive value with its reference string
12301|                    result[reference_string] = value;
12302|                    break;
12303|                }
12304|            }
12305|        }

12307|        /*!
12308|        @param[in] value  flattened JSON
12309|
12310|        @return unflattened JSON
12311|        */
12312|        static basic_json unflatten(const basic_json& value)
12313|        {
12314|            if (not value.is_object())
12315|            {
12316|                JSON_THROW(std::domain_error("only objects can be unflattened"));
12317|            }
12318|
12319|            basic_json result;
12320|
12321|            // iterate the JSON object values
12322|            for (const auto& element : *value.m_value.object)
12323|            {
12324|                if (not element.second.is_primitive())
12325|                {
12326|                    JSON_THROW(std::domain_error("values in object must be primitive"));
12327|                }
12328|
12329|                // assign value to reference pointed to by JSON pointer; Note
12330|                // that if the JSON pointer is "" (i.e., points to the whole
12331|                // value), function get_and_create returns a reference to
12332|                // result itself. An assignment will then create a primitive
12333|                // value.
12334|                json_pointer(element.first).get_and_create(result) = element.second;
12335|            }
12336|
12337|            return result;
12338|        }

12569|    attributes are missing); example: `"operation add must have member path"`
12570|
12571|    @complexity Linear in the size of the JSON value and the length of the
12572|    JSON patch. As usually only a fraction of the JSON value is affected by
12573|    the patch, the complexity can usually be neglected.
12574|
12575|    @liveexample{The following code shows how a JSON patch is applied to a
12576|    value.,patch}
12577|
12578|    @sa @ref diff -- create a JSON patch by comparing two JSON values
12579|
12580|    @sa [RFC 6902 (JSON Patch)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6902)
12581|    @sa [RFC 6901 (JSON Pointer)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901)
12582|
12583|    @since version 2.0.0
12584|    */
12585|    basic_json patch(const basic_json& json_patch) const
12586|    {
12587|        // make a working copy to apply the patch to
12588|        basic_json result = *this;
12589|
12590|        // the valid JSON Patch operations
12591|        enum class patch_operations {add, remove, replace, move, copy, test, invalid};
12592|
12593|        const auto get_op = [](const std::string & op)
12594|        {
12595|            if (op == "add")
12596|            {
12597|                return patch_operations::add;
12598|            }
12599|            if (op == "remove")
12600|            {
12601|                return patch_operations::remove;
12602|            }
12603|            if (op == "replace")
12604|            {
12605|                return patch_operations::replace;
12606|            }
12607|            if (op == "move")
12608|            {
12609|                return patch_operations::move;
12610|            }
12611|            if (op == "copy")
12612|            {
12613|                return patch_operations::copy;
12614|            }
12615|            if (op == "test")
12616|            {
12617|                return patch_operations::test;
12618|            }
12619|
12620|            return patch_operations::invalid;
12621|        };
12622|
12623|        // wrapper for "add" operation; add value at ptr
12624|        const auto operation_add = [&result](json_pointer & ptr, basic_json val)
12625|        {
12626|            // adding to the root of the target document means replacing it
12627|            if (ptr.is_root())
12628|            {
12629|                result = val;
12630|            }
12631|            else
12632|            {
12633|                // make sure the top element of the pointer exists
12634|                json_pointer top_pointer = ptr.top();
12635|                if (top_pointer != ptr)
12636|                {
12637|                    result.at(top_pointer);
12638|                }
12639|
12640|                // get reference to parent of JSON pointer ptr
12641|                const auto last_path = ptr.pop_back();
12642|                basic_json& parent = result[ptr];
12643|
12644|                switch (parent.m_type)
12645|                {
12646|                    case value_t::null:
12647|                    case value_t::object:
12648|                    {
12649|                        // use operator[] to add value
12650|                        parent[last_path] = val;
12651|                        break;
12652|                    }
12653|
12654|                    case value_t::array:
12655|                    {
12656|                        if (last_path == "-")
12657|                        {
12658|                            // special case: append to back
12659|                            parent.push_back(val);
12660|                        }
12661|                        else
12662|                        {
12663|                            const auto idx = std::stoi(last_path);
12664|                            if (static_cast<size_type>(idx) > parent.size())
12665|                            {
12666|                                // avoid undefined behavior
12667|                                JSON_THROW(std::out_of_range("array index " + std::to_string(idx) + " is out of range"));
12668|                            }
12669|                            else
12670|                            {
12671|                                // default case: insert add offset
12672|                                parent.insert(parent.begin() + static_cast<difference_type>(idx), val);
12673|                            }
12674|                        }
12675|                        break;
12676|                    }
12677|
12678|                    default:
12679|                    {
12680|                        // if there exists a parent it cannot be primitive
12681|                        assert(false);  // LCOV_EXCL_LINE
12682|                    }
12683|                }
12684|            }
12685|        };
12686|
12687|        // wrapper for "remove" operation; remove value at ptr
12688|        const auto operation_remove = [&result](json_pointer & ptr)
12689|        {
12690|            // get reference to parent of JSON pointer ptr
12691|            const auto last_path = ptr.pop_back();
12692|            basic_json& parent = result.at(ptr);
12693|
12694|            // remove child
12695|            if (parent.is_object())
12696|            {
12697|                // perform range check
12698|                auto it = parent.find(last_path);
12699|                if (it != parent.end())
12700|                {
12701|                    parent.erase(it);
12702|                }
12703|                else
12704|                {
12705|                    JSON_THROW(std::out_of_range("key '" + last_path + "' not found"));
12706|                }
12707|            }
12708|            else if (parent.is_array())
12709|            {
12710|                // note erase performs range check
12711|                parent.erase(static_cast<size_type>(std::stoi(last_path)));
12712|            }
12713|        };
12714|
12715|        // type check
12716|        if (not json_patch.is_array())
12717|        {
12718|            // a JSON patch must be an array of objects
12719|            JSON_THROW(std::invalid_argument("JSON patch must be an array of objects"));
12720|        }
12721|
12722|        // iterate and apply the operations
12723|        for (const auto& val : json_patch)
12724|        {
12725|            // wrapper to get a value for an operation
12726|            const auto get_value = [&val](const std::string & op,
12727|                                          const std::string & member,
12728|                                          bool string_type) -> basic_json&
12729|            {
12730|                // find value
12731|                auto it = val.m_value.object->find(member);
12732|
12733|                // context-sensitive error message
12734|                const auto error_msg = (op == "op") ? "operation" : "operation '" + op + "'";
12735|
12736|                // check if desired value is present
12737|                if (it == val.m_value.object->end())
12738|                {
12739|                    JSON_THROW(std::invalid_argument(error_msg + " must have member '" + member + "'"));
12740|                }
12741|
12742|                // check if result is of type string
12743|                if (string_type and not it->second.is_string())
12744|                {
12745|                    JSON_THROW(std::invalid_argument(error_msg + " must have string member '" + member + "'"));
12746|                }
12747|
12748|                // no error: return value
12749|                return it->second;
12750|            };
12751|
12752|            // type check
12753|            if (not val.is_object())
12754|            {
12755|                JSON_THROW(std::invalid_argument("JSON patch must be an array of objects"));
12756|            }
12757|
12758|            // collect mandatory members
12759|            const std::string op = get_value("op", "op", true);
12760|            const std::string path = get_value(op, "path", true);
12761|            json_pointer ptr(path);
12762|
12763|            switch (get_op(op))
12764|            {
12765|                case patch_operations::add:
12766|                {
12767|                    operation_add(ptr, get_value("add", "value", false));
12768|                    break;
12769|                }
12770|
12771|                case patch_operations::remove:
12772|                {
12773|                    operation_remove(ptr);
12774|                    break;
12775|                }
12776|
12777|                case patch_operations::replace:
12778|                {
12779|                    // the "path" location must exist - use at()
12780|                    result.at(ptr) = get_value("replace", "value", false);
12781|                    break;
12782|                }
12783|
12784|                case patch_operations::move:
12785|                {
12786|                    const std::string from_path = get_value("move", "from", true);
12787|                    json_pointer from_ptr(from_path);
12788|
12789|                    // the "from" location must exist - use at()
12790|                    basic_json v = result.at(from_ptr);
12791|
12792|                    // The move operation is functionally identical to a
12793|                    // "remove" operation on the "from" location, followed
12794|                    // immediately by an "add" operation at the target
12795|                    // location with the value that was just removed.
12796|                    operation_remove(from_ptr);
12797|                    operation_add(ptr, v);
12798|                    break;
12799|                }
12800|
12801|                case patch_operations::copy:
12802|                {
12803|                    const std::string from_path = get_value("copy", "from", true);;
12804|                    const json_pointer from_ptr(from_path);
12805|
12806|                    // the "from" location must exist - use at()
12807|                    result[ptr] = result.at(from_ptr);
12808|                    break;
12809|                }
12810|
12811|                case patch_operations::test:
12812|                {
12813|                    bool success = false;
12814|                    JSON_TRY
12815|                    {
12816|                        // check if "value" matches the one at "path"
12817|                        // the "path" location must exist - use at()
12818|                        success = (result.at(ptr) == get_value("test", "value", false));
12819|                    }
12820|                    JSON_CATCH (std::out_of_range&)
12821|                    {
12822|                        // ignore out of range errors: success remains false
12823|                    }
12824|
12825|                    // throw an exception if test fails
12826|                    if (not success)
12827|                    {
12828|                        JSON_THROW(std::domain_error("unsuccessful: " + val.dump()));
12829|                    }
12830|
12831|                    break;
12832|                }
12833|
12834|                case patch_operations::invalid:
12835|                {
12836|                    // op must be "add", "remove", "replace", "move", "copy", or
12837|                    // "test"
12838|                    JSON_THROW(std::invalid_argument("operation value '" + op + "' is invalid"));
12839|                }
12840|            }
12841|        }
12842|
12843|        return result;
12844|    }

12846|    /*!
12847|    @brief creates a diff as a JSON patch
12848|
12849|    Creates a [JSON Patch](http://jsonpatch.com) so that value @a source can
12850|    be changed into the value @a target by calling @ref patch function.
12851|
12852|    @invariant For two JSON values @a source and @a target, the following code
12853|    yields always `true`:
12854|    @code {.cpp}
12855|    source.patch(diff(source, target)) == target;
12856|    @endcode
12857|
12858|    @note Currently, only `remove`, `add`, and `replace` operations are
12859|          generated.
12860|
12861|    @param[in] source  JSON value to compare from
12862|    @param[in] target  JSON value to compare against
12863|    @param[in] path    helper value to create JSON pointers
12864|
12865|    @return a JSON patch to convert the @a source to @a target
12866|
12867|    @complexity Linear in the lengths of @a source and @a target.
12868|
12869|    @liveexample{The following code shows how a JSON patch is created as a
12870|    diff for two JSON values.,diff}
12871|
12872|    @sa @ref patch -- apply a JSON patch
12873|
12874|    @sa [RFC 6902 (JSON Patch)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6902)
12875|
12876|    @since version 2.0.0
12877|    */
12878|    static basic_json diff(const basic_json& source,
12879|                           const basic_json& target,
12880|                           const std::string& path = "")
12881|    {
12882|        // the patch
12883|        basic_json result(value_t::array);
12884|
12885|        // if the values are the same, return empty patch
12886|        if (source == target)
12887|        {
12888|            return result;
12889|        }
12890|
12891|        if (source.type() != target.type())
12892|        {
12893|            // different types: replace value
12894|            result.push_back(
12895|            {
12896|                {"op", "replace"},
12897|                {"path", path},
12898|                {"value", target}
12899|            });
12900|        }
12901|        else
12902|        {
12903|            switch (source.type())
12904|            {
12905|                case value_t::array:
12906|                {
12907|                    // first pass: traverse common elements
12908|                    size_t i = 0;
12909|                    while (i < source.size() and i < target.size())
12910|                    {
12911|                        // recursive call to compare array values at index i
12912|                        auto temp_diff = diff(source[i], target[i], path + "/" + std::to_string(i));
12913|                        result.insert(result.end(), temp_diff.begin(), temp_diff.end());
12914|                        ++i;
12915|                    }
12916|
12917|                    // i now reached the end of at least one array
12918|                    // in a second pass, traverse the remaining elements
12919|
12920|                    // remove my remaining elements
12921|                    const auto end_index = static_cast<difference_type>(result.size());
12922|                    while (i < source.size())
12923|                    {
12924|                        // add operations in reverse order to avoid invalid
12925|                        // indices
12926|                        result.insert(result.begin() + end_index, object(
12927|                        {
12928|                            {"op", "remove"},
12929|                            {"path", path + "/" + std::to_string(i)}
12930|                        }));
12931|                        ++i;
12932|                    }
12933|
12934|                    // add other remaining elements
12935|                    while (i < target.size())
12936|                    {
12937|                        result.push_back(
12938|                        {
12939|                            {"op", "add"},
12940|                            {"path", path + "/" + std::to_string(i)},
12941|                            {"value", target[i]}
12942|                        });
12943|                        ++i;
12944|                    }
12945|
12946|                    break;
12947|                }
12948|
12949|                case value_t::object:
12950|                {
12951|                    // first pass: traverse this object's elements
12952|                    for (auto it = source.begin(); it != source.end(); ++it)
12953|                    {
12954|                        // escape the key name to be used in a JSON patch
12955|                        const auto key = json_pointer::escape(it.key());
12956|
12957|                        if (target.find(it.key()) != target.end())
12958|                        {
12959|                            // recursive call to compare object values at key it
12960|                            auto temp_diff = diff(it.value(), target[it.key()], path + "/" + key);
12961|                            result.insert(result.end(), temp_diff.begin(), temp_diff.end());
12962|                        }
12963|                        else
12964|                        {
12965|                            // found a key that is not in o -> remove it
12966|                            result.push_back(object(
12967|                            {
12968|                                {"op", "remove"},
12969|                                {"path", path + "/" + key}
12970|                            }));
12971|                        }
12972|                    }
12973|
12974|                    // second pass: traverse other object's elements
12975|                    for (auto it = target.begin(); it != target.end(); ++it)
12976|                    {
12977|                        if (source.find(it.key()) == source.end())
12978|                        {
12979|                            // found a key that is not in this -> add it
12980|                            const auto key = json_pointer::escape(it.key());
12981|                            result.push_back(
12982|                            {
12983|                                {"op", "add"},
12984|                                {"path", path + "/" + key},
12985|                                {"value", it.value()}
12986|                            });
12987|                        }
12988|                    }
12989|
12990|                    break;
12991|                }
12992|
12993|                default:
12994|                {
12995|                    // both primitive type: replace value
12996|                    result.push_back(
12997|                    {
12998|                        {"op", "replace"},
12999|                        {"path", path},
13000|                        {"value", target}
13001|                    });
13002|                    break;
13003|                }
13004|            }
13005|        }
13006|
13007|        return result;
13008|    }
